name_zh: 提斯塔谷茶园大吉岭红茶
processing: Darjeeling tea, with orthodox making typical of the district. Oxidation depends on the flush.
harvest_season: Not recorded in detail for this garden. As across Darjeeling, picking runs through spring, summer and autumn flushes.
appearance_dry: Typically twisted olive-brown leaf with some tips.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber, depending on the flush.
taste_profile: The garden's cup is little documented. As with other Darjeelings, spring lots lean floral and summer lots lean fruity and rounder.

brewing.notes: A standard Western-style Darjeeling brew works; drop the temperature a little for spring lots.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush under the garden's name, mainly abroad. Current-season lots are the norm, and spring tea is best young.
description:
Teesta Valley is a Darjeeling garden and village in the Rangli Rangliot block, 10 km from Takdah. It is a sizeable community, with a little over 6,000 residents at the 2011 census, and its tea goes to Japan, Europe and elsewhere.

How the garden makes its tea is not well documented. Darjeeling gardens typically work in orthodox style, and the leaf changes considerably from flush to flush.

Typical of the district, a spring lot is light and floral, a summer lot fuller and fruitier. Taste as you go and do not assume every lot from one garden behaves the same.

Buy by flush and year. Since the garden's name is also a place, make sure the label means the estate and not just a loose regional reference.
history: The founding year usually given is 1841, which would make it very early, as that is also the year tea was first planted in the Darjeeling area; that date is worth treating with some caution. The garden is now owned by Bharat Bajaria.
